beaver.intro: A northern Lake Michigan island trip is a calendar decision. See passenger and standard vehicle fares, sailing-season variability and why car reservations matter.
notes: Beaver Island Boat Company publishes a date-by-date 2026 calendar with one to four departures depending on the day. There is no safe single 'daily ferry time'.
All vehicles and trailers require reservations; passenger reservations are generally not required.
Vehicle quote below covers only a standard vehicle under 7 ft 6 in high and no more than 16 ft long. Oversize cars, trailers, bikes and kayaks have separate published rates.

decisions: Passengers are first-come
The company does not take passenger reservations. Arrive early enough to buy tickets, handle bags and park.
Vehicle space is separate
Reserve a car well ahead. The operator requires earlier check-in for vehicles than the basic passenger allowance.
Watch the time ashore
Four hours of round-trip sailing can leave a short island visit. Enter two real sailings and see the remaining window.
guide: A day around St. James
Keep the plan close to the arrival harbor unless you have confirmed an island tour or transport. The whole island will not fit into a short gap between boats.
Staying overnight
Arrange lodging and mainland overnight parking. The parking shuttle is for drivers; drop passengers and luggage at the dock first.
Exploring beyond the harbor
Choose a rental, tour or your own reserved vehicle before you arrive. Match what you carry to the operator’s luggage and freight categories.

Reserve vehicle space if taking a car

faq: Can I reserve seats for the family?
The operator says passenger travel is first-come, first-served rather than reserved. Vehicle transport does require separate arrangements.
How early should I check in?

The passenger FAQ asks for at least an hour. Vehicle reservations require at least 90 minutes, with additional time for some racks or freight situations. The timeline adjusts its allowance when a vehicle is selected.

A bike or family outing

A vehicle that really needs to go

decisions: Book the right vehicle
Measure length and height with attachments. The simple fare reference is for the standard low-car category; other sizes need a fresh operator quote.
Be checked in an hour ahead
The operator requires reservation holders to check in at the booth at least one hour before departure. Parking at the terminal is not the same as checking in.
Match both ends of Highway 6
A ferry booking needs a land plan on both sides. Leave room after arrival before another time-sensitive stop.
guide: A Manitoulin road trip
South Baymouth is the arrival point, not every island destination. Add your own onward driving allowance and avoid building the day around an assumed immediate departure.
Foot passengers
Think through transport after arrival. Confirm the correct sailing and any terminal parking charge before leaving your vehicle behind.
RVs, propane and pets
Use the operator’s current size and dangerous-goods rules, including propane limits. Ask about pet areas and boarding assistance when booking.
checklist: Reserve with Ontario Ferries for the correct direction

Reach the ticket booth at least one hour before sailing

faq: Is this the Manitou Island ferry from Leland?
No. Chi-Cheemaun serves Manitoulin Island in Ontario. North and South Manitou are separate islands in Michigan’s Sleeping Bear Dunes National Lakeshore.
Is the crossing always 1 hour 45 minutes?
The operator describes about 1 hour 45 minutes in peak season and about 2 hours off-peak. The timeline uses that seasonal distinction.

toronto.note: This public passenger planner does not provide general automobile transport. Teenagers ages 15–19 and seniors have separate fares; use the official city pricing for those categories.

Tickets include the return journey. Last boats vary by landing and season; confirm city schedule, especially after dusk.
The city warns of long peak-season queues. Online tickets provide an express entrance line, not a reserved departure seat.
steps: Select the island destination by your itinerary, not simply the shortest line.
Choose the date: winter sailings only reach Ward's Island on the published seasonal schedule.
Check departure and last-return times; allow queue time on sunny summer weekends.

decisions: A ticket is not a reserved place
Buying online can save time in the ticket line, but does not make a crowded ferry a guaranteed departure.
Return from a different dock
City tickets cover the return from any operating island dock. Build a walk across the islands if the timetable supports it.
Winter changes the map
The published winter period uses Ward’s Island. Centre and Hanlan’s should not appear as available simply because their docks exist.
guide: A family day near Centre
Pick the dock for the places you actually want to visit, and check those attractions separately. Keep a margin for the return queue.
A quieter arrival at Ward’s
Consider the longer walk before choosing an alternate dock. A shorter queue is not a promise, and a longer walk may not suit every group.
A skyline and shoreline walk
Use one dock outward and another for the return only after checking that both operate. Keep the departure terminal and island dock names in your saved plan.
checklist: Check which island routes operate on your date
Use Jack Layton terminal, not the island-airport ferry
Allow for ticket, boarding and island return queues
Choose a return dock that fits the day’s walking
faq: Do I need to return from the same dock?
No. The city says its tickets include the return from any island dock. That dock still needs to have service when you want to leave.
Is the Billy Bishop airport ferry the same service?
No. This planner is for the city’s Toronto Island ferries departing from Jack Layton Ferry Terminal.

The mainland–Pelee calculator uses 2026 published fares in Canadian dollars. Sandusky is an international route with separate fares and limited dates.
The final planned 2026 sailing is December 7; winter island air service is a different system.
steps: Choose a date before driving: the Canadian mainland boarding location changes during the season.
Check Sandusky eligibility and border requirements separately if coming from the United States.
Confirm vehicle dimensions and round-trip availability; reserve exact sailings before departure.

The 2026 calendar shifts the regular mainland gateway to Kingsville from July 29. Special sailings can still differ.
Reserve the return as well
Pelee requires reservations for foot passengers and vehicles. A trip to the island is not a guaranteed ride back.
Canada and Sandusky are different trips
Sandusky is an international crossing with different sailing dates, fares and document requirements. The fare calculator here covers the Canadian-mainland route.
guide: A day on two wheels
Decide how you will reach the places you want to see before you choose a walk-on ticket. Pack for exposure to wind and sun, and leave a return margin.
Taking a vehicle
Reserve the actual vehicle and passenger group. Let the operator know if you need boarding assistance or a vessel with an elevator.
An international visit
Use the dedicated Sandusky schedule and current border guidance. Do not use a Canadian-mainland fare as an international quote.
checklist: Read the terminal name on each direction of the booking
Reserve both outward and return travel
Check in at the booth at least one hour before sailing
For Sandusky, verify the international timetable and documents
extraSources: Pelee reservation, check-in and accessibility information
faq: Why did the planner change my mainland port?
The regular 2026 schedule uses Leamington earlier in the season and Kingsville from July 29. Verify your exact sailing because exceptions exist.
Does this estimate cover Sandusky?
No. It covers the Canadian mainland–Pelee route only. Sandusky has distinct international fares, dates and border requirements.

Queen IV departs Copper Harbor for Rock Harbor in about 3.5 hours. Sea Hunter III is oriented to Windigo; Voyageur II serves multiple island landing points.
There are no car ferries. NPS requires matching inbound/outbound transportation and appropriate national park permits.

Choose a gateway based on driving distance, trip length, and whether a round trip can fit your dates.

A backpacking route

decisions: Watch the clock labels
Westbound arrival looks one hour earlier on the clock; eastbound looks one hour later. Travel duration stays the same.
Make room before sailing
Boarding opens roughly 90 minutes ahead and gates close 15 minutes before sailing. This planner starts with a 90-minute arrival allowance.
Passengers and car are separate
Taking a vehicle does not include the people inside it. Check the actual vehicle dimensions, including racks.
guide: Taking the car across
Measure the vehicle with its attachments. Move medication, a warm layer and anything needed during the crossing into your carry-on before leaving the vehicle deck.
Walking on for a city break
Plan onward transport on both shores. A ferry terminal is a starting point, not automatically a downtown hotel stop.
Compare the whole travel day
Enter your own drive-around time below to compare it with check-in, sailing and unloading. This is elapsed-time arithmetic, not a live road-traffic estimate.
checklist: Book passengers and vehicle separately as needed
Bring government-issued photo identification
Verify vehicle size, including roof and rear racks
Put needed items in your carry-on before boarding

faq: Do Lake Express schedules use local time?
Read each port’s local-time label. Muskegon is Eastern Time; Milwaukee is Central Time. The planner displays both.
Can I go back to my car while underway?
Lake Express says passengers cannot access the vehicle deck during the crossing. Bring what you need into the cabin.

decisions: Four hours really means four
The clock difference can disguise the duration. Treat the ship as a substantial part of the travel day.
Choose a pace, not just a fare
Badger and Lake Express depart from different cities. Compare the land connections and the kind of crossing you want.
Keep the shore plan flexible
A published season is not confirmation of today’s operation. Check the operator before driving to either terminal.
guide: Make a voyage of it
Keep a layer, your camera and a small day bag with you. Leave room to settle into the crossing rather than filling every arrival minute with another commitment.
Taking your vehicle
Confirm the operator’s current vehicle handling and oversize rules. Include a realistic unload-and-depart allowance before scheduling the onward drive.
Arriving without a car
Start with the terminal address and arrange the next leg before you board. Use the route map to understand which side of each town you are arriving on.
checklist: Check the exact date on the Badger calendar
Verify your departure port and its time zone
Confirm vehicle handling and any special dimensions
Leave room after arrival for unloading and onward travel
faq: Is the westbound trip only three hours?
No. The crossing is about four hours. Wisconsin clocks are one hour behind Michigan clocks.
Is Badger the same ferry as Lake Express?
No. Badger connects Ludington and Manitowoc. Lake Express connects Muskegon and Milwaukee. The ports and crossing experiences differ.

decisions: 2026: no regular ferry
Manitou Island Transit says no trips to either island in 2026 while NPS relocates the docks. Do not drive to Leland expecting a departure.
2027: expected is not confirmed
NPS anticipates reopening the docks and villages in 2027. A construction target is not a ferry timetable, fare or ticket.
Private access has its own limits
NPS describes offshore landings and authorized charter access, with no dock or protected anchoring. This tool does not recommend a private-boat substitute.
guide: South Manitou: history and a bounded island visit

The lighthouse and village help explain why people came to this island. Their 2026 closure matters to the experience, even if a visitor has a permitted way ashore. Use the South Manitou NPS page to check precisely what reopens.
North Manitou: room for a backcountry stay
Choose it for the kind of trip you prepare for rather than a quick photo stop. Transport, a backcountry permit and a water plan are separate pieces of preparation.
Build a future plan without buying certainty

Save your preferred island and trip style now. Confirm the NPS reopening notice, then the ferry operator’s new schedule, then any permit or campsite arrangements before making a nonrefundable commitment.

faq: Is the entire island closed in 2026?

NPS describes limited access and specific closures, including docks, villages and potable water; South Manitou has additional facility closures. The regular ferry does not operate. Consult the current NPS notice for exact boundaries.
Can I book the 2027 ferry now?
This planner has no verified 2027 ferry timetable or fares. NPS’s expected dock reopening is not an operator restart confirmation.
Is Manitoulin the same place?
No. Ontario’s Manitoulin Island is served by Chi-Cheemaun. Michigan’s North and South Manitou Islands are part of Sleeping Bear Dunes National Lakeshore.
